```{r setup-descriptives, include=FALSE}
library(here)

                      fig.width = 7, dpi = 110)
```

# Purpose of this document

This report is an **item check** of the main study, not a substantive analysis. For every survey
item it shows a simple descriptive plot so I can inspect whether the items
behave as intended: Did respondents understand the question? Does the phrasing
push people towards a particular answer? Are the response options being used?
No scales are computed and no hypotheses are tested here.

**Everything is weighted** with the trimmed survey weight `w`, unless a chart or
table says otherwise. Counts are weighted counts (sums of weights; the weights
average 1, so they read as respondents) and every *n* beside them is the
unweighted number of respondents.

**How labels are handled.** Question wording comes from the variable labels in
the agency's `.sav`, answer labels from the agency's codebook
(`analysis/assets/NLOZ26-10_Timo_Drugsbeleid_codebook_261014.xlsx`), whose labels
`analysis/R/00_load_and_clean.R` puts on the columns.

**Where the data comes from.** `analysis/data/` holds the agency's export, which
carries no names or panel identifiers beyond an interview id; it is not
version controlled.

:::: {.block-box}
**Provenance of the input files.**

- `analysis/data/NLOZ26-10_Drugsbeleid_gedeeld_261022.sav` — the full main
  study, delivered 22 October 2026: the completed interviews, with survey
  weights.
- `analysis/assets/NLOZ26-10_Timo_Drugsbeleid_codebook_261014.xlsx` — the
  agency's codebook, the source of the answer labels.
- `analysis/R/00_load_and_clean.R` — all cleaning and every derived variable,
  shared with the rest of the repository; `analysis/R/utils/report_helpers.R` —
  the helper functions of this report.
::::

# Data cleaning

All cleaning happens in `analysis/R/00_load_and_clean.R`, the same script the
paper uses, and **everything in this report — all three tabs — reads its
result, `df`**: the `r nrow(df)` completed interviews that carry a survey weight.
*Geen mening* (code 99) is a missing answer on every item, not a reason to
remove the respondent; on the 0-100 involvement sliders 99 is a position on the
scale and is kept.

### The emotion question

The agency exports the emotion question as **one binary variable per emotion ×
topic** — the form an attitude network needs, where each emotion is its own
node. `00_load_and_clean.R` names them `emo_<topic>_<feeling>` (e.g.
`emo_hard_worried`; 1 = ticked, 0 = not ticked, `NA` = the topic was not
answered) and adds one column per topic, `emo_<topic>`, holding the combination
of feelings ticked (e.g. `"worried + happy"`), for the combination charts below.

### One analysis dataset

`df` has one row per analysed respondent, every variable typed once and every
derived variable computed once. That is the dataset the rest of this report
reads, and the one a network analysis should use: each belief, behaviour,
policy item and emotion binary is a candidate node, and the grouping variables
are covariates.

```{r dataset-shape, echo=TRUE}
# What `df` contains, by column group.
groups <- list(
  `policy (beleid_voorkeur_*)`      = grep("^beleid_voorkeur_", names(df), value = TRUE),
  `beliefs + behaviour`             = c(select_items("beliefs"), select_items("gedrag")),
  `reverse-scored copies (_scored)` = grep("_scored$", names(df), value = TRUE),
  `own use (gebruik_*)`             = select_items("gebruik"),
  `involvement (+ mean)`            = c(select_items("betrokkenheid"), "betrokkenheid_mean"),
  `emotion x topic binaries`        = grep("^emo_[a-z]+_[a-z]+$", names(df), value = TRUE),
  `emotion combinations`            = paste0("emo_", emo_topics),
  `derived groupings`               = c("substance_ladder", "mdma_support", "vote_lr", "vote_3"))
tibble::tibble(`column group` = c(names(groups), "everything else (ids, demographics, weights, ...)"),
               columns = c(lengths(groups), ncol(df) - length(unlist(groups)))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("`df`: ", nrow(df), " respondents x ", ncol(df), " columns"))
```

:::: {.block-box}
**What the export tells us about the data.** Worth keeping in mind when reading
everything below:

- **"Geen mening" is code 99** on the policy question, the belief and behaviour
  statements and the practice questions. It is missing in `df`.
- **The policy question stores whole rules**, 1 (verbod) to 9 (vrije verkoop).
  No answer lies between two rules.
- **The involvement block has five sliders**, `betrokkenheid_1`, `_1b`, `_2`,
  `_2b` and `_3`, all analysed.
- **Demographics are the agency's recodes**, labelled by the agency's `.sav`.
::::

Every plot and every analysis is based on the same `r nrow(df)` people; the *n*
per item can be lower where someone chose *geen mening*. Every answer option is
shown even if nobody chose it.

# 2. Beleidsvoorkeur, opvattingen, gedrag, gebruik, emoties en betrokkenheid

```{r political-split-sizes, echo=TRUE}
# The largest and smallest vote group (left / middle / right; unweighted n), named in the paragraph below.
vote_sizes <- table(df$vote_3)
n_links  <- max(vote_sizes); n_links_code  <- names(which.max(vote_sizes))
n_rechts <- min(vote_sizes); n_rechts_code <- names(which.min(vote_sizes))
```

:::: {.block-box}
All item questions are drawn below. Two things are worth knowing.

**The charts are interactive.** Use the buttons to split every question by
**demografie**, **middelengebruik** or **MDMA-regulering**; the button colours
mark the families.

Because the groups differ in size, the grouped splits show the **weighted
percentage within each group** rather than counts — otherwise the comparison
would mostly reflect how many people are in each group. The **emotion charts
are the exception and show weighted counts**: that question allows more than
one answer, so a respondent can appear in several bars at once and the bars do
not add up to the group. The **as:** button switches the remaining charts
between the two. Age is shown as **stacked weighted counts**, so each bar keeps
its total height while showing its age composition. **Stemherinnering** is
grouped as in Figure 3 of the paper: left, middle or right by the party's
position in the Chapel Hill Expert Survey 2024; other parties, blank and
non-voters fall outside that split. Respondents who
fall outside a split (a missing code, or *geen mening* on the MDMA question) are
excluded from that view and counted underneath it.

**Group sizes.** The legend prints the unweighted *n* of every group beside its
colour, and it is worth reading: the groups differ a great deal in size
(stemherinnering `r n_links_code`: `r n_links`, `r n_rechts_code`:
`r n_rechts`), so a percentage in a small group rests on a handful of
respondents and moves several points if one of them answers differently.
Comparisons between the small groups are indicative at best.

**Two question types get extra treatment.** The policy question is shown in its
**nine rules** plus *geen mening*. Substance use carries an explicit
**"overgeslagen"** category so refusals stay visible rather than disappearing.
::::

:::: {.block-box}
**Definition of the splits made in `00_load_and_clean.R`.** Own use is asked
for four substance **groups** &mdash; alcohol, tabak (en vapes), softdrugs and
harddrugs &mdash; each with the same four answers: **nooit gebruikt**, **niet
in het laatste jaar**, **wel eens in het laatste jaar** and **vaak in het
laatste jaar**.

**middelengebruik** (`substance_ladder`) is the heaviest group a respondent has
*ever* used, whatever the frequency:

| groep | definitie |
|:--|:--|
| **nooit** | never used any of the four groups |
| **legaal** | alcohol or tabak, never softdrugs or harddrugs |
| **softdrugs** | softdrugs, never harddrugs |
| **harddrugs** | harddrugs |

Each label names the **heaviest** group a respondent reaches, so someone in
*harddrugs* may also drink.

**MDMA-regulering** (`mdma_support`) is *voor* for rule 5 (alleen in
speciaalzaak, zonder winst) or freer on the MDMA policy question, *tegen*
otherwise.
::::

:::: {.block-box}
**No emotion splits.** The emotion question allows more than one answer per
topic, so groups formed from it overlap: a respondent who ticked two emotions
would sit in two bars, and the bars would not sum to anything. The emotion
answers themselves are drawn in section 2.5.
::::

### Elke combinatie van emoties

Every distinct combination a respondent actually gave, per topic — so a mixed
answer such as *bang / bezorgd + blij* is visible as its own response option
rather than being split across two bars.

```{r emotion-combinations, echo=TRUE, fig.height=3.4}
# One horizontal bar per observed combination (`emo_<topic>` from 00_load_and_clean.R), weighted.
for (t in emo_topics) {
  combo <- df[[paste0("emo_", t)]]
  ok <- !is.na(combo)
  combo_nl <- vapply(strsplit(combo[ok], " + ", fixed = TRUE),
                     \(z) paste(tolower(emo_lab$feeling[z]), collapse = " + "), "")
  tab <- tibble(combination = combo_nl, w = df$w[ok]) |>
    summarise(n = sum(w), .by = combination) |>
    arrange(n) |>
    mutate(combination = factor(combination, levels = combination))
  print(
    ggplot(tab, aes(x = n, y = combination)) +
      geom_col(fill = "#3B6EA5", width = 0.75) +
      geom_text(aes(label = round(n)), hjust = -0.3, size = 3, colour = "grey20") +
      scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
      scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(38)) +
      labs(title = paste0("Emotiecombinaties — ", emo_lab$topic[[t]]),
           subtitle = paste0(nrow(tab), " verschillende combinaties, n = ", sum(ok),
                             " respondenten; balken gewogen"),
           x = "aantal respondenten (gewogen)", y = NULL) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9),
            panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()))
}
```

```{r descriptives-cube, include=FALSE}
# ---- The counts cube behind the interactive charts -------------------------------
# For every item, the weighted count of each answer category, overall and within every group of every
# split. Sending counts rather than responses makes the split buttons instant and keeps respondent-level
# data out of the HTML. Group sizes go along twice: `n` (unweighted, for the legend) and `nw` (weighted, the
# denominator of the percentages).
dem <- build_splits()

split_rows <- function(spec, g) !is.na(spec$assign) & spec$assign == g

counts_by_group <- function(codes, k) {
  out <- list(all = round(w_tabulate(codes, df$w, k), 2))
  for (d in names(dem))
    out[[d]] <- lapply(seq_along(dem[[d]]$groups), \(g)
      round(w_tabulate(codes[split_rows(dem[[d]], g)], df$w[split_rows(dem[[d]], g)], k), 2))
  out
}

# weighted density of a continuous item, scaled to weighted counts (density x weight sum x binwidth), so it
# is comparable with the bars. Empty coordinates for a group of fewer than three respondents.
density_by_group <- function(values, from, to, binwidth, n_points = 96) {
  curve <- function(x, w) {
    ok <- !is.na(x)
    if (sum(ok) < 3) return(list(x = numeric(0), y = numeric(0)))
    d <- stats::density(x[ok], weights = w[ok] / sum(w[ok]), from = from, to = to, n = n_points)
    list(x = round(d$x, 2), y = round(d$y * sum(w[ok]) * binwidth, 2))
  }
  out <- list(all = curve(values, df$w))
  for (d in names(dem))
    out[[d]] <- lapply(seq_along(dem[[d]]$groups), \(g)
      curve(values[split_rows(dem[[d]], g)], df$w[split_rows(dem[[d]], g)]))
  out
}

desc_blocks <- list()

# ---- ordered Likert blocks ----
for (spec in list(list("beliefs", "Opvattingen (beliefs)"), list("gedrag", "Gedrag"))) {
  cols  <- select_items(spec[[1]])
  scale <- answer_scale(cols[1])
  items <- lapply(seq_along(cols), \(i) {
    codes <- match(as.numeric(df[[cols[i]]]), scale$code)
    list(title  = numbered_titles(cols)[i],
         mean   = round(w_mean(codes, df$w), 2),
         sd     = round(w_sd(codes, df$w), 2),
         counts = counts_by_group(codes, nrow(scale)))
  })
  desc_blocks[[length(desc_blocks) + 1]] <- list(id = spec[[1]], title = spec[[2]], categories = scale$label,
                                                 orderable = TRUE, items = items)
}

# ---- substance use: an explicit "skipped" category ----
cols  <- select_items("gebruik")
scale <- answer_scale(cols[1])
items <- lapply(seq_along(cols), \(i) {
  codes <- match(as.numeric(df[[cols[i]]]), scale$code)
  valid <- codes
  codes[is.na(codes)] <- nrow(scale) + 1L          # blank -> the skipped bin
  list(title  = numbered_titles(cols)[i],
       mean   = round(w_mean(valid, df$w), 2),
       sd     = round(w_sd(valid, df$w), 2),
       counts = counts_by_group(codes, nrow(scale) + 1L))
})
desc_blocks[[length(desc_blocks) + 1]] <- list(id = "gebruik", title = "Middelengebruik",
                                               categories = c(scale$label, "overgeslagen"),
                                               orderable = TRUE, items = items)

# ---- policy: the nine rules + "Geen mening" ----
cols  <- grep("^beleid_voorkeur_", names(df), value = TRUE)
scale <- answer_scale(cols[1])
items <- lapply(seq_along(cols), \(i) {
  val   <- as.numeric(df[[cols[i]]])
  codes <- match(val, scale$code)
  codes[is.na(val)] <- nrow(scale) + 1L            # NA = "Geen mening"
  list(title  = item_titles(cols)[i],
       counts = counts_by_group(codes, nrow(scale) + 1L))
})
# the colours of the nine rules in main.tex (01_fig_policy_preferences.R: viridis, end = 0.9), grey for
# "Geen mening"
desc_blocks[[length(desc_blocks) + 1]] <- list(id = "beleid_voorkeur", title = "Beleidsvoorkeur",
                                               categories = c(scale$label, "Geen mening"),
                                               catColours = c(substr(viridisLite::viridis(9, end = 0.9), 1, 7),
                                                              "#BBBBBB"),
                                               items = items)

# ---- involvement sliders: five equal-width bins + density ----
cols <- select_items("betrokkenheid")
nb   <- 5
ed   <- seq(0, 100, length.out = nb + 1)
items <- lapply(seq_along(cols), \(i) {
  val <- as.numeric(df[[cols[i]]])
  list(title   = item_titles(cols)[i],
       counts  = counts_by_group(pmin(floor(val / (100 / nb)) + 1L, nb), nb),
       density = density_by_group(val, from = 0, to = 100, binwidth = 100 / nb))
})
desc_blocks[[length(desc_blocks) + 1]] <- list(id = "betrokkenheid", title = "Betrokkenheid",
                                               categories = paste0(ed[-length(ed)], "–", ed[-1]),
                                               anchorPos = (ed[-length(ed)] + ed[-1]) / 2,
                                               hasDensity = TRUE, items = items)

# ---- emotions: weighted number ticking each feeling, per topic ----
items <- lapply(emo_topics, \(t) {
  cls <- paste0("emo_", t, "_", emo_feelings)
  wsum <- \(rows) round(vapply(cls, \(cl) sum(df$w[rows] * df[[cl]][rows], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1)), 2)
  cnt <- list(all = unname(wsum(rep(TRUE, nrow(df)))))
  for (d in names(dem))
    cnt[[d]] <- lapply(seq_along(dem[[d]]$groups), \(g) unname(wsum(split_rows(dem[[d]], g))))
  list(title = unname(emo_lab$topic[[t]]), counts = cnt)
})
desc_blocks[[length(desc_blocks) + 1]] <- list(id = "emotions", title = "Emoties",
                                               categories = unname(emo_lab$feeling), multi = TRUE, items = items)

# ---- group sizes: unweighted n (legend), weighted nw (percentages), and how many fall outside ----
dem_out <- lapply(dem, \(spec) list(
  label = spec$label, mode = spec$mode, groups = spec$groups,
  n  = vapply(seq_along(spec$groups), \(g) sum(split_rows(spec, g)), integer(1)),
  nw = round(vapply(seq_along(spec$groups), \(g) sum(df$w[split_rows(spec, g)]), numeric(1)), 2),
  overlapping = FALSE,
  excluded = sum(is.na(spec$assign))))

desc_data <- list(N = nrow(df), NW = round(sum(df$w), 2), demographics = dem_out, blocks = desc_blocks)
```

```{r descriptives-data, echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
# The cube is built in the hidden chunk above; this chunk hands it to the
# browser, together with the script that draws the charts.
cat('<script>window.DESC_DATA = ',
    jsonlite::toJSON(desc_data, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 3, na = "null"),
    ';</script>', sep = '')
cat('<script>', paste(browser_js("descriptives"), collapse = "\n"), '</script>', sep = '\n')
```
